assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational account of collateral constraints and amplification that transformed macro-finance and policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore provide the core collateral-cycle mechanism; Gertler's work is central to the financial-accelerator formulation and dissemination.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been extensively developed, empirically studied and used in modern monetary and macroprudential analysis.
uncertainties: The contribution overlaps with a broad literature on credit frictions, making the precise laureate boundary difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work supplied influential tools for understanding liquidity, search, intermediation and price formation in modern financial markets.
assessment.attribution: Duffie and the Pedersen-Garleanu collaboration made distinct and complementary contributions to the core search-based asset-market literature.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are mature, widely adopted and highly relevant to the organization and fragility of over-the-counter markets.
uncertainties: The broad finance literature contains several closely related contributors whose exclusion would require careful justification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection changed the analysis of trade, productivity and the distributional effects of globalization.
assessment.attribution: Melitz introduced the canonical heterogeneous-firm framework; Helpman and Redding made major related theoretical and empirical advances.
assessment.maturity: The approach is deeply embedded in trade research and has generated a large empirical and policy literature.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among foundational heterogeneous-firm and broader new-trade-theory contributors is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on household leverage and mortgage debt substantially improved understanding of financial crises and aggregate demand.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are especially closely identified with the central empirical account; Campbell's household-finance contributions provide important foundations.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been repeatedly investigated and remain central to analysis of credit booms, defaults and macroeconomic stabilization.
uncertainties: The literature's causal interpretation and the appropriate boundary between household finance and macro-finance remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The combination of theory and credible measurement made insurance-market selection empirically tractable and policy relevant.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein and Einav made leading empirical contributions, while Salanie supplied influential theoretical and econometric foundations.
assessment.maturity: The work has produced a durable research program across health, annuity and other insurance markets.
uncertainties: It is difficult to separate the most decisive contributions from a wider body of insurance and contract-theory research.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This literature established liquidity and funding constraints as central determinants of asset prices and systemic stress.
assessment.attribution: Amihud's measurement work and the theoretical contributions of Pedersen and Brunnermeier are identifiable pillars of the field.
assessment.maturity: Its mechanisms are well established and have become standard in research on market disruptions and intermediary balance sheets.
uncertainties: Substantial overlap with other liquidity, intermediary and market-microstructure contributions complicates a discrete award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative Ricardian models gave researchers a disciplined way to measure trade gains and conduct counterfactual policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Kortum is central to the quantitative Ricardian tradition, with Costinot and Rodriguez-Clare providing major analytical and welfare advances.
assessment.maturity: The methods are extensively used and have had durable influence on applied international-trade research.
uncertainties: Its conceptual debt to earlier Ricardian and quantitative-trade work complicates attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement and analysis of management practices revealed an important, actionable source of productivity differences across firms and countries.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen developed the core measurement program; Sadun made major contributions to its extension and interpretation.
assessment.maturity: A large cross-country evidence base and subsequent experimental work support the importance of the research agenda.
uncertainties: Questions remain about the generality and causal interpretation of measured management practices.
